props.title: Hanussen

sections.content: István Szabó's Hanussen stands as a haunting exploration of power, manipulation and rising fascism in pre-WWII Europe. Klaus Maria Brandauer delivers a mesmerizing performance as Erik Jan Hanussen, the real-life clairvoyant who rose to prominence in 1930s Berlin. The film forms the final part of Szabó's unofficial trilogy examining power and identity, following Mephisto (1981) and Colonel Redl (1985). Like those masterworks, Hanussen delves into how individuals navigate treacherous political waters while losing their moral compass.

sections.content: The film's prescient warnings about the seduction of authoritarianism connect strongly to other European works examining the rise of fascism. The Conformist (1970) similarly explores how individuals become complicit in totalitarian systems, while Cabaret (1972) uses Berlin's decadent entertainment scene to show society's descent into Nazism. Szabó's direction maintains an eerie, dreamlike quality that enhances the supernatural elements while grounding them in historical reality.

Hanussen's abilities as a clairvoyant serve as a powerful metaphor for both the appeal and danger of charismatic leadership. Like The Seventh Seal (1957) and Hour of the Wolf (1968), the film uses supernatural elements to probe deeper psychological and societal truths. The protagonist's journey from circus performer to influential political figure parallels Germany's own transformation from fragile democracy to fascist state. sections.content: The film's examination of power dynamics connects to other works about psychics and mentalists who gain dangerous influence. The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari (1920) similarly used a hypnotist character to comment on authority and control in German society. Rasputin and the Empress (1932) explored another real historical figure who used supposed supernatural abilities to gain political power. Szabó's achievement lies in making these themes resonate both as specific historical commentary and universal warning about the dangers of charismatic manipulation.
